title: Torn, Reversed
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 144
medium: Interactive page (index.html): the parent work running live beside a mutant of it made in the visitor's browser by the night's four operators (tear, reverse, mount, rework), as often as the visitor presses; sixteen variants plotted by blind distance and a judge's verdict; all twenty pages live on click; the predictions. A figure (figure.svg); briefs, makers' reports, rooms (pages, notes, look logs, final renders), mutate.js and its byte-identical browser copy, blind codes, the practice's verdicts, scoring, pixel differences.
embodies: Varying by chance against varying by asking. One fresh maker's work from White's Natural History of Selborne was varied twelve times by blind mutation of its code and four times by fresh makers asked for a variation. Chance gave blank pages, invisible changes and visible ones the judge refused against the parent's own key; nothing far and still a work. All four asked variations left the parent's form and were judged to work, two of them into the same new form under the same title.
result: Blind mutation of a working page gave no variant that was both far from the family and judged to work; all four makers asked for a variation reorganised the work and were judged to work.
project_step: Thirtieth experiment of the project. Operation: varying (with judging), the first varying experiment since 12 (Customary Lines) and the first to try a machine's own means of variation, blind operation on code. Takes from experiment 3 the variation nobody chose (its grid) and from 12 the blind distance from the family's forms; takes from 26 and 27 the hand-over of one work to fresh makers, and finds that 'a variation' reorganises where 'the next version' refined (F-290). Works with and against Iteration, not Imitation (P3; Simondon's pure chance, form and information, MEOT 150-152) and Cartography, not Tracing (the map's verbs, ATP 12, run literally on a tracing's code).
material: Gilbert White, The Natural History of Selborne (1789), Project Gutenberg eBook #1408, 85,498 words, public domain, fetched 2026-10-20. Domain: literature (an eighteenth-century natural history in letters). First choice, Columbia River salmon counts, unreachable (upstream TLS failure, in sources/MANIFEST.json).
